courses.name: Statics and Solid Mechanics
courses.description: Applies statics and material mechanics to forces, stresses and deformation in structures.
courses.prerequisites: (( MATH 1342 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M with a minimum grade of D- ); ( PHYS 1151 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 261M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 1161 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- )) or ( PHYS 1141 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 1241 with a minimum grade of D- )

courses.name: Recitation for CIVE 2221
courses.description: Provides guided problem solving in statics and solid mechanics.

courses.name: Environmental Measurements in Natural and Engineered Systems
courses.description: Develops environmental measurement, data analysis and reporting through field and laboratory work.
courses.prerequisites: CHEM 1151 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 233M with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1161 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1211 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Lab for CIVE 2300
courses.description: Investigates environmental measurement through experiments and a project.

courses.name: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics
courses.description: Applies fluid mechanics and conservation principles to hydraulic systems and experiments.
courses.prerequisites: CIVE 2221 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Environmental Engineering: Principles, Technology, and Sustainability
courses.description: Introduces environmental assessment, treatment technologies, pollution control and waste management.

courses.description: Models pollutant movement, transformation and persistence in water, soil and air.

courses.description: Develops the design of physical, chemical and biological water-treatment processes.
courses.prerequisites: ( CIVE 2331 with a minimum grade of D- or CHME 2310 with a minimum grade of D- ); CIVE 2334 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Lab for CIVE 4534
courses.description: Investigates water-treatment concepts through laboratory experiments.

courses.name: Senior Design Project—Environmental
courses.description: Develops an environmental engineering design in teams with faculty/practitioner guidance and presentations to stakeholders.
courses.prerequisites: ( CIVE 5536 with a minimum grade of D- or CIVE 4534 with a minimum grade of D- ); (ENGW 3301 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3302 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3315 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 3301 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 3302 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 3315 with a minimum grade of C )

courses.name: Resource Recovery and Waste Treatment Technologies Abroad
courses.description: Examines waste treatment, recycling and resource recovery through study abroad and design projects.

courses.name: Climate Hazards and Resilient Cities Abroad
courses.description: Studies climate hazards, data analysis and urban resilience through an international comparison.

courses.name: Equity in Engineering
courses.description: Examines equity, environmental justice and community impacts of engineering decisions.

courses.name: Climate and Atmospheric Change
courses.description: Examines climate-system change using historical evidence, data and predictive models.
courses.prerequisites: ENVR 1200 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 2200 with a minimum grade of D- or (( PHYS 1151 with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 261M with a minimum grade of D- ); ( PHYS 1152 with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 26LM with a minimum grade of D- ); ( PHYS 1153 with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 26SM with a minimum grade of D- )) or graduate program admission

courses.description: Models organic contaminants across environmental media and examines ecological risks.
courses.prerequisites: CHEM 1151 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 233M with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1211 with a minimum grade of D- or graduate program admission

courses.name: Tools and Techniques of Environmental Health
courses.description: Examines environmental-health exposures, risk assessment and approaches to prevention.

courses.name: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
courses.description: Applies fluid mechanics, observation and modeling to environmental flows.

courses.name: Dynamic Modeling for Environmental Investment and Policymaking
courses.description: Builds dynamic models for environmental policy and investment decisions under uncertainty.

courses.name: Solid and Hazardous Waste Management
courses.description: Examines waste-management engineering, alternatives, regulation and socioeconomic considerations.

courses.name: Life Cycle Assessment of Materials, Products, and Infrastructure
courses.description: Models product and infrastructure life cycles to evaluate environmental and health impacts.
courses.prerequisites: CIVE 3464 with a minimum grade of D- or graduate program admission

courses.name: Remote Sensing of the Environment
courses.description: Develops satellite-data analysis and environmental remote-sensing methods.

courses.name: Coastal Dynamics and Design
courses.description: Examines coastal dynamics, hazards and design of built and nature-based coastal defenses.
courses.prerequisites: CIVE 2331 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 3120 with a minimum grade of D- or graduate program admission; Additional course-description condition: one semester of fluid mechanics or equivalent.

courses.name: Climate Science, Engineering Adaptation, and Policy
courses.description: Connects climate science, engineering adaptation, infrastructure resilience and policy choices.

courses.name: Climate Technologies for Decarbonization, Mitigation, and Adaptation
courses.description: Evaluates climate-mitigation and adaptation technologies, their feasibility, costs and trade-offs.

courses.name: Air Quality Engineering and Science
courses.description: Examines atmospheric chemistry, air pollution, environmental effects and energy solutions.

courses.name: Air Quality Management
courses.description: Models air pollutants and evaluates emission controls, health effects and standards.
courses.prerequisites: CIVE 2334 with a minimum grade of D- or graduate program admission

courses.name: Atmospheric Boundary Layer Flows
courses.description: Studies atmospheric turbulence, surface exchange and methods of measurement and simulation.
courses.prerequisites: ( CIVE 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; ( MATH 2321 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M with a minimum grade of D- ); PHYS 1161 with a minimum grade of D- ) or graduate program admission

courses.name: Hydrologic and Hydraulic Design
courses.description: Applies hydrology and hydraulic models to drainage and flood-control design.
courses.prerequisites: ( CIVE 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; (ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C )) or graduate program admission

courses.name: Global Biogeochemistry
courses.description: Examines global elemental cycles and their relationships with human activity and climate.

courses.name: Special Topics in Civil Engineering
courses.description: Studies a department-approved civil-engineering topic offered in response to identified needs.

courses.name: Energy Systems: Science, Technology, and Sustainability
courses.description: Examines energy technologies, infrastructure, efficiency and sustainability trade-offs.
courses.prerequisites: ( MATH 1241 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1250 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1341 with a minimum grade of D- ) or MATH 21EM with a minimum grade of D- ; ( PHYS 1151 with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 261M with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 1161 with a minimum grade of D- or PHYS 1171 with a minimum grade of D- )

courses.name: Engineering Microbiology and Ecology
courses.description: Examines microorganisms and ecological processes in natural and engineered environmental systems.
courses.prerequisites: CHEM 1151 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 233M with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1161 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1211 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Ecosystems Ecology
courses.description: Studies ecosystem energy flows, elemental cycles and human impacts.
courses.prerequisites: BIOL 1107 with a minimum grade of D- or BIOL 1111 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1161 with a minimum grade of D- or CHEM 1214 with a minimum grade of D- or EEMB 2302 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 1200 with a minimum grade of D- or ENVR 2200 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 1
courses.description: Introduces engineering design and programming through projects, laboratories and an original design solution.

courses.name: Cornerstone of Engineering 2
courses.description: Continues project-based engineering design with analysis, programming, ethical reasoning and working prototypes.
courses.prerequisites: GE 1501 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or ENGR 150M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Discrete Structures
courses.description: Develops discrete structures, logic, proofs and counting methods for computing.

courses.name: Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
courses.description: Introduces programming, dataset analysis and ethical issues in software design.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2000
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting introductory programming coursework.

courses.name: Program Design and Implementation 1
courses.description: Develops program design, object-oriented abstractions and software engineering practices.

courses.name: Lab for CS 2100
courses.description: Provides experiments supporting program design coursework.

courses.name: Introduction to Databases
courses.description: Develops relational database design, SQL and introductory database-system techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 200M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 201M with a minimum grade of D- or CS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2000 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D- or EECE 2560 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.description: Develops robust software architectures and data pipelines using substantial datasets.
courses.prerequisites: CS 2100 with a minimum grade of D- or DS 2500 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Studies the mathematical basis of AI through linear algebra, probability and computational exercises.

courses.name: Information Presentation and Visualization

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Introduces predictive modeling and major supervised and unsupervised learning methods.
courses.prerequisites: DS 3000 with a minimum grade of D- or CIS 250M with a minimum grade of D- or ( MATH 2331 with a minimum grade of D- ; MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- )

courses.name: General Chemistry for Engineers

courses.name: Recitation for CHEM 1151
courses.description: Provides guided discussion and practice for engineering chemistry.

courses.name: Calculus 1 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops differentiation, its scientific applications, and introductory integration.

courses.name: Calculus 2 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Continues integration methods, series, and introductory vectors and spatial motion.
courses.prerequisites: Additional course-description condition: MATH 1341 or permission of head mathematics advisor.

courses.name: Calculus 3 for Science and Engineering
courses.description: Develops multivariable differentiation, multiple integrals and vector calculus.

courses.name: Differential Equations and Linear Algebra for Engineering
courses.description: Combines differential-equation methods and linear algebra for engineering applications.

courses.name: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Develops probability distributions and limit theory, then introduces statistical inference.
courses.prerequisites: MATH 1342 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1252 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1242 with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Physics for Engineering 1

courses.prerequisites: MATH 1241 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1251 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1340 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1341 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 21EM with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 1342 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 211M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 2321 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 316M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

courses.name: Lab for PHYS 1151

courses.name: Interactive Learning Seminar for PHYS 1151
courses.description: Practices mathematical problem solving in mechanics and fluids.

courses.name: Dynamic Earth
courses.description: Studies Earth materials, geological processes and landscapes through plate tectonics.

courses.name: Earth's Changing Cycles
courses.description: Examines interacting Earth systems, human disturbances and sustainability responses.

courses.name: Global Oceanic Change
courses.description: Examines ocean change across timescales and its environmental and social implications.
courses.prerequisites: Additional course-description condition: one laboratory science course or permission of instructor.

courses.name: Water Resources
courses.description: Examines hydrology, water quality, resource management and water-use conflicts.

courses.name: Oceanography
courses.description: Integrates ocean processes and examines marine-system responses to human pressures.

courses.name: Introduction to Engineering Co-op Education

courses.prerequisites: ENGW 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1111 with a minimum grade of C or WRIT 201M with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1102 with a minimum grade of C or ENGL 1111 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1113 with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 1114 with a minimum grade of C
